entries.detail: Hegemony Inquisition (House of Questions) arrives atop the Apex. White-robed Brides of Truth walk with mute black-robed Grooms whose proboscises suck lies from skulls. People vanish at night. Even Lonrot and Loonflower are not immune.
A preacher called the Rainmaker stirs the populace against the Water Baron, promising free water falling from the sky as it did in myth. Mobs gather and wail in public squares.
The Hegemon recalls all Legions to the heartlands. House Lonrot holds the city with only their household guard. Prime moment for Gnomonian independence.

A reckless vault-raider released a Titan-era language virus. Sufferers endlessly repeat a mantra; hearing the chant risks infection. Citizens stuff ears with wax and ring every bell in the city to drown out the infected. Philosopher's Guilds race for a cure.
A fire rages (or recently devastated) a swathe of the city's townhouses. An NPC the party is close to has lost their home or is in imminent danger. Cause uncertain — possibly deliberate.
The Faa Clans' once-in-a-decade Great Moot. Tent-metropolis outside the walls dwarfs Gnomon itself. Marriages arranged, ritual duels end with both dead, souks filled with deep-desert bounty.

entries.description: Matter-fabricating cocoon. Creates a randomly generated creature from local encounter table, neurally altered to love the user (treat as Pet).

entries.name: Hard Light Projector
entries.description: Projects flat wide bridge of weightless hard light, range ten feet. Walkable.

entries.name: Hover Boots
entries.description: Antigravity boots. Brief sojourns into thin air.

entries.name: Hushboots
entries.description: Sable footwear that silences footsteps. ADV when sneaking or attacking blind creatures.

entries.name: Instant Table
entries.description: Elegant dining table compressed via hypergeometry to matchbox size. Unfurls when thrown to ground. Cannot be folded again.

entries.name: Mirror Shield
entries.description: +1 AV. DEX Save to reflect beam attacks back at source.

entries.name: Mord-Red's Grail
entries.description: Liquids poured into this silver goblet become deadly poison (d12 TOX).

entries.name: Moonbeast Carapace
entries.description: Flayed carapace of a Moonbeast. Wearer has AV 16, immunity to radiation. Once worn, cannot be removed.

entries.name: Phase Cape
entries.description: Hypergeometric cloth. Wearer slips out of lucid reality for d4 rounds. Cannot be touched, cannot touch others. Still visible.

entries.name: Presence Drone
entries.description: Small floating sphere announces one's presence in pompous voice. DIS on encounter rolls. Impossible to hide. Once activated, must be destroyed or traded away.

entries.name: Spirit Prison (Empty)
entries.description: Manifold crystal prison for paradoxical creatures. Empty. Thrown at Hypergeometric or Outsider, EGO Save or trapped forever, released at bearer's pleasure.

entries.name: Spirit Prison (Occupied)
entries.description: As Spirit Prison but already holds a Paradoxical Outsider (roll on that table to determine entity).

entries.name: Sprayflesh
entries.description: Canister sprays healing pseudoflesh. Remove 1 Wound from Biological target per use.

entries.name: Starskin
entries.description: Biomechanoid space-suit of antiquity. AV 16, immunity to suffocation, free movement in antigravity.

entries.name: Ulfire Lantern
entries.description: Shines ulfire light. See through solid objects and be seen. Blocked by lead.

entries.name: Universal Ration
entries.description: Thick white nutrient-cake. Full heal for Biological creatures.

entries.name: Ammunition Fabricator
entries.description: Refills ammunition for any ranged weapon in your possession.

entries.name: Ardent Maggots
entries.description: Gourd of synthetic grubs. Strip a corpse to bone in seconds. Will not eat live flesh.

entries.name: Autarch's Fork
entries.description: Obsidian dining fork glows green when stuck into poison.

entries.name: Autarch's Nectar
entries.description: Honeyed golden tonic with gene-sculpting nanomachines. Drunk by a Biological creature: permanent +1 to three Ability scores.

entries.name: Babel Bomb
entries.description: Neuro-active grenade. Living creatures in blast cannot understand or produce coherent language for a day.

entries.name: Bedazzling Blade
entries.description: Off-handed parrying sword (d6) of the Fallen Autarchy. Blade glows sun-bright on demand. Opponents DEX Save vs d6 rounds Blindness.

entries.name: Blue Rust
entries.description: Alchemical compound. Turns metal to rust within moments. d6 CON damage to Synthetic creatures per round.

entries.name: Bottled Thicket
entries.description: Vial of weaponised seeds. Broken, seeds sprout into iridescent vines within seconds. Fills room, strangles all living creatures d8/round. STR Save to break free.

entries.name: Ditto Gun
entries.description: Revolver. Bullets create temporal anomalies that inflict a wound identical to the target's most recent injury, with matching damage value.

entries.name: Gecko Gloves
entries.description: Nano-cloth gloves. Hands stick to any flat surface with near-unbreakable grip. Climb impossible distances.

entries.name: Hedondroid
entries.description: Factory-sealed synthetic partycrasher. Crude alcohol-powered android, locates parties/orgies/weddings within five-day radius. Joins party as a Follower.

entries.name: Lazarus Cap
entries.description: +1 AV. Necrotech helm. Applied to fresh corpse, re-activates the brain. Effect only lasts while cap worn; does nothing to arrest flesh decay (wearer loses d4 CON per day).

entries.name: Magnetic Orb
entries.description: Large silver orb emits powerful magnetic field. All nearby metal objects and Synthetic-type creatures are irresistibly drawn to it.

entries.name: Mind Shield
entries.description: +1 AV. Golden cage worn around head. Protects from psychic intrusion. Cannot use Mystic Gifts. Exempt from Gleam Tests.

entries.name: Not-Sword
entries.description: Sword (d8) engraved with paradoxical LogLang glyphs. Synthetic creatures cannot recognise this as a blade, nor recognise the bearer as a living being.

entries.name: Phase Grenades
entries.description: Physical objects in blast briefly de-synched with reality; others pass through like mist. Brief, harmless.

entries.name: Philosopher's Dirk
entries.description: Neuroactive dagger. d4 INT damage per stab. At 0 INT victim adopts your point of view.

entries.name: Prison Orb of the Miniature Beast
entries.description: Hypergeometric orb, scarlet/pallid hemispheres. 4-in-6 chance still contains a Citrine-coated Volt Rat trained to kill; 2-in-6 chance holds desiccated corpse of forgotten beast.

entries.name: Psybernetic Helm
entries.description: +1 AV. First time worn, installs a random Mystic Gift.

entries.name: Quantum Umbilical
entries.description: Links destiny of two creatures. While one lives, the other cannot truly die.

entries.name: Tech Wand
entries.description: Silver wand. Re-activate or deactivate a piece of arcane technology.

entries.name: Tempest Cannon
entries.description: Creates incredibly violent localised thunderstorms wherever shells explode (d12, blast, electrical). Reload with 3 rations of water.

entries.name: The Book of Sand
entries.description: Hypergeometric book, infinite pages, infinite tiny illegible paragraphs each. Decoding impossible. Infinite length could fuel an endless fire.

entries.name: The Crimson Cantos
entries.description: Crimson-bound volume of poetry. Neuro-active. Readers EGO save or violently attack the nearest living creature.

entries.name: Watchful Ferret
entries.description: Small golden synthetic ferret. Sits on shoulder, nips you when it detects unseen danger. Does not eat or breathe.

entries.name: Anti-Gravity Field Generator
entries.description: Tetrahedron of black metal. Excludes Urth's gravity within throwing distance. Creatures not adapted to zero-G must DEX Save to move or float helplessly.

entries.name: Biotic Field Generator
entries.description: Golden beacon. Planted on floor, emits healing nanomachine cloud for 6 rounds. All Biological creatures in melee range regain +d10 HP per round in cloud.

entries.name: Black Cloud Bomb
entries.description: Releases nanomachine cloud that consumes biological matter, d6 unblockable damage per round. Cloud grows by +d6 per kill until no biological matter remains, then hibernates.

entries.name: Cybernetics Pack
entries.description: Factory-sealed cybernetic implant (generate randomly).

entries.name: Demiurge Crayon
entries.description: Hypergeometric artefact resembling a child's crayon. Any item, creature, or object drawn becomes real.

entries.name: Disguise Ring
entries.description: Holographic disguise. Projects hologram around wearer. Visual replica only — touch reveals deception. Pre-loaded with disguise from local encounter table.

entries.name: Fate Inverter
entries.description: Paradox-device. Activated, all nearby failed Saves become successes and vice versa; missed attacks hit, hits miss.

entries.name: Horror Helm
entries.description: +2 AV. Autarch's war-helm. Activated, bellows neuroactive threats. All Biological foes in earshot Morale Save or flee.

entries.name: Huntsman Fly
entries.description: Cocoon with synth-fly. Given a drop of blood/DNA, unerringly locates target. Dies on mission complete.

entries.name: Quantum Daemon Horn
entries.description: Sound draws attention of a Greater Quantum Daemon. They arrive immediately and are bound to perform one boon.

entries.name: Lithling Seed
entries.description: Corpse/embryo of a Lithling. Immersed in correct chemical bath, slowly crystallizes into adult Lithling.

entries.name: Manifold Box
entries.description: Hypergeometric box larger inside than outside. Holds 10 slots of items weightlessly. Retrieving in combat takes an action.

entries.name: Pale Fire
entries.description: Wooden flask, hueless flame from extradimensional anti-ember. Burns bitterly cold, consumes metal and water. Extinguished by oil or flammable liquid.

entries.name: Philosopher's Bridge
entries.description: Creates pair of round hypergeometric portals on solid walls (one blue, one orange). Pass through like mundane apertures, momentum retained. User may close portals at will.

entries.name: Scatter-Shoal Ring
entries.description: Activated, projects 9 hard-light holograms of wearer scattering in all directions. Solid, react when 'hurt', cannot speak. Opponents 1-in-10 chance to target real wearer.

entries.name: Snakemaker
entries.description: Gun fires synthetic snakes (Lvl 0, AV 11, d4 bite). Do not like or obey wielder.

entries.name: Stormcaller
entries.description: Accursed flute. Played beneath open sky, a Prismatic Tempest forms overhead.

entries.name: TALLHAT Amplifier
entries.description: Psionic amplifier hidden in black conical hat. Worn: +1 to all mental stats. Identifies one as a Witch of the Mooncradle Mountains.

entries.name: Thinking Cap
entries.description: +1 AV, +2 INT. If wearer was not previously sentient, becomes so.

entries.name: Titancreed Fragment: KILL
entries.description: Fragment of Titan AI language. Read aloud, all Synthetic creatures in hearing range EGO Save or fly into killing frenzy.

entries.name: Titancreed Fragment: OBEY
entries.description: Read aloud, all Synthetic creatures in hearing range EGO Save or obey one verbal command from the reader.

entries.name: Titancreed Fragment: SLEEP
entries.description: Read aloud, all Synthetic creatures in hearing range EGO Save or fall into resting state.

entries.name: Vimana Map
entries.description: Crystal chunk. Activated, projects holographic map guiding user to a lost Autarch's Vimana.

entries.name: Wind-up Haruspex
entries.description: Clockwork fortune teller. Given entrails/stomach of recently-butchered animal or person, discerns likely future. One question at a time. Answers YES, NO, or PERHAPS.

rolling_tables.notes: [INT] = reader's INT bonus.

entries.name: Antithetical Copy
entries.effect: Creates a daemonic, insanely evil copy of a target entity. The copy is alive and violently opposed to the existence of the original - if it makes physical contact with the original, both entities are explosively destroyed. The antithesis crumbles to ash after [INT] hours.

entries.name: Diminish
entries.effect: Target shrinks to half original size and mass. Lasts [INT] hours.

entries.name: Erase Paradox
entries.effect: Targeted Hypergeometric or Outsider-type entity must EGO save vs 10+[INT]. On failure: entity accepts its fundamental implausibility and ceases to exist.

entries.name: Exchange Coordinates
entries.effect: Reader swaps physical position with a targeted entity. Mishap = stuck together.

entries.name: Expand
entries.effect: Target grows to double original size and mass. Lasts [INT] hours.

entries.name: Flatten
entries.effect: Target transformed into a 2D hypergeometric entity. Lasts [INT] hours.

entries.name: Golem
entries.effect: Imbues an inanimate object with mobility and sentience. Lives [INT] hours. Reaction Roll for disposition.

entries.name: Imperfect Copy
entries.effect: Creates [INT] copies of a target entity. Colourless and lifeless, resembling ash sculptures.

entries.name: Increase Gravity
entries.effect: Target feels gravity at 10x usual force. Unable to move or fight. Lasts [INT] combat rounds.

entries.name: Invert Gravity
entries.effect: Target's gravitational polarity reversed for [INT] combat rounds. Falls skyward. When effect ends: d6 falling damage per round they fell skywards.

entries.name: Kinetic Ward
entries.effect: Invisible wall negating all physical attacks. Protects one entity for [INT] combat rounds, or [INT] entities for one combat round.

entries.name: Perfect Copy
entries.effect: Perfect copy of a target entity. Resembles original in all respects. Crumbles to ash after [INT] hours.

entries.name: Phase
entries.effect: Target placed out of sync with reality. Visible but cannot touch anything (except other phased entities). Lasts [INT] combat rounds.

entries.name: Portal
entries.effect: Creates paired linked portals on two flat surfaces in line of sight. Persist [INT] combat rounds.

entries.name: Return Fixed Coordinates
entries.effect: Reader and/or [INT] other entities transported to a predetermined point. Codex connects to one pre-written location.

entries.name: Return Random Coordinates
entries.effect: Reader and/or [INT] other entities transported to a random point previously occupied.

entries.name: Singularity
entries.effect: Miniature black hole for [INT] combat rounds. Draws in all unsecured entities. Engulfed = destroyed. Living beings must STR save vs 10+[INT] to avoid.

entries.name: Stasis
entries.effect: Single entity stranded outside the flow of time for [INT] combat rounds. Cannot be moved, harmed, or interacted with.

entries.name: Summon
entries.effect: Plucks a creature from the manifold halls of creation. Roll Monster Generator tables. Reaction Roll as normal.

entries.name: Vanish
entries.effect: Target no longer visible in normal light spectrum. Infrared still detects. Lasts [INT] hours.

entries.name: Accelerate
entries.effect: Target moves at double speed for [INT] combat rounds, makes twice normal attacks.

entries.name: Assert Normality
entries.effect: Circle of enforced normality, free of space-time aberrations. Lasts [INT] combat rounds. Hypergeometric/Outsider creatures physically repelled, cannot enter. Mystic Gifts and distortion-Exotica cannot be used inside.

entries.name: Attraction
entries.effect: Target attracts objects of same type (glass attracts glass, etc.) as though magnetised. Lasts [INT] hours.

entries.name: Blink
entries.effect: Teleport to location in line of sight. Mishap = stuck inside nearby physical object.

entries.name: Create Cube
entries.effect: Creates cube [INT] feet in height/depth, wholly comprised of any material reader can currently touch. Slot weight = [INT].

entries.name: Darkness
entries.effect: Jet of complete darkness. Blinds [INT] creatures for d6 combat rounds. Light sources caught inside permanently extinguished.

entries.name: Dismantle
entries.effect: Target separated into constituent parts, grouped by caster's whim (colour, size, material, etc.). Living targets: EGO save vs 10+[INT] to resist.

entries.name: Freeze
entries.effect: Localised supercoolant cloud dealing [INT]d6 DEX damage to target. At 0 DEX: frozen solid, cannot move until thawed.

entries.name: Invert Fate
entries.effect: Target's destiny inverted. Failed saves/attacks become successes, successes become failures. Lasts [INT] combat rounds.

entries.name: Klein Bottle
entries.effect: Paradoxical hypergeometric bottle containing [INT] doses of any fluid, even unsafe ones (magma, acid, sable ikor).

entries.name: Labyrinth Seed
entries.effect: Fissure leading to Vaarn's hypergeometric Labyrinth. Permanent, grows in size over time.

entries.name: Map of Fate
entries.effect: Roll [INT]d20. Whenever any PC or NPC makes a dice roll, must choose from these d20 results. No other dice can be rolled until pool expended. Using again before expended = immediate Mishap.

entries.name: Pale Fire
entries.effect: Impossible pale fire that exclusively burns non-flammable materials. Extinguished by flammable gases/liquids.

entries.name: Phantasms
entries.effect: Up to [INT] light-distortion anomalies appearing as solid objects or living creatures. No weight/depth, don't match ambient light.

entries.name: Psychometry
entries.effect: Attune to full 4D shape of a held object. Ask Referee [INT] Yes or No questions about object's past, present, and possible futures.

entries.name: Radiance
entries.effect: Searing flash of blinding red sunlight. All nearby creatures with eyes: DEX save vs [INT] rounds of Blindness.

entries.name: Reflective Ward
entries.effect: Hyper-reflective surface (hand-mirror size). Reflects up to [INT] attacks of any type back at source before breaking. Lasts one combat round.

entries.name: Repel
entries.effect: Target repels objects of same type (anti-magnetised). Lasts [INT] hours.

entries.name: Sever
entries.effect: Severs one of target's body parts from the whole. For [INT] hours, severed part moves separately but operates normally (eyes see, hands grasp, etc.).

entries.name: Web
entries.effect: Target entangled in hypergeometric threads for [INT] rounds, or [INT] entities entangled for one round. Lose -5 AV, cannot move.

rolling_tables.notes: Roll on natural 1 when reciting an equation. [INT] = reader's INT bonus.

entries.name: Antithesis
entries.effect: Births a daemonic, insanely evil copy of the reader, with their Level and HP. Violently opposed to the reader; physical contact = both entities explosively destroyed. Exists for [INT] combat rounds.

entries.name: Brainstorm
entries.effect: Reader's muddled thoughts actualise as polychrome lightning from eyes and mouth. Everyone nearby takes 2d6 electrical damage, DEX save for half.

entries.name: Chroma-shadow
entries.effect: Reader's shadow permanently shifts in hue, becoming pinkish-orange.

entries.name: Codex Collapse
entries.effect: The hypergeometric codex collapses in on itself, vanishing from existence.

entries.name: Entropy-withered
entries.effect: Reader's body twists and decays under entropic hypergeometric forces. Lose d6 maximum HP, cannot regain.

entries.name: Giant Item
entries.effect: An inventory item is subjected to hypergeometric forces, becoming enormous. Item's weight in slots triples. Roll d10 for slot affected. Permanent.

entries.name: Gigantism
entries.effect: Reader's body grows uncontrollably, swelling to fill the room. Occupants must evacuate or be crushed. Outdoors, growth continues for full duration. Lasts [INT] hours, then steady deflation.

entries.name: Inverted Anatomy
entries.effect: Reader's internal organs placed on the outside, clothing inside. AV becomes 10, doubled damage from all sources. Lasts [INT] days.

entries.name: Inverted Fate
entries.effect: Reader's destiny inverted. All failed Saves and attack rolls become successes and vice versa. Lasts [INT] days.

entries.name: Labyrinth Pox
entries.effect: Reader contracts Labyrinth Pox, a hypergeometric ailment.

entries.name: Lost Past
entries.effect: Reader permanently loses a chunk of history. PC loses one Level, subtracts d8 HP from max, reduces Ability scores by three points.

entries.name: Petrified
entries.effect: Reader's body freezes under crushing hypergeometric force. Cannot move or act for [INT] hours.

entries.name: Planeyfied
entries.effect: Reader becomes a 2D hypergeometric being. See Planeyfolk ancestry. Lasts [INT] days.

entries.name: Quantum Daemon
entries.effect: A paradoxical quantum daemon is called into existence. Displeased, wishes the reader ill.

entries.name: Revelation
entries.effect: Reader witnesses a terrible vista in a higher-order dimension. d6 damage to INT, PSY, and EGO.

entries.name: Shrunken Head
entries.effect: Reader's head subjected to hypergeometric forces, becoming minute. Body retains size. Gains Wound: Shrunken Head. Lose d6 INT, PSY, EGO. Cannot wear helmets or hats.

entries.name: Space-Time Vortex
entries.effect: Mispronunciation creates a rupture vomiting inanimate debris and living creatures. Roll once on local encounter table each combat round; creature is ejected at high velocity with rubble (DEX save to avoid).

entries.name: Spirit Hand
entries.effect: Reader's left hand permanently drawn into a hypergeometric dimension. Left arm ends in a strange blue fissure; missing hand feels immersed in cold television static. Take d10 DEX damage. Unarmed attacks with the missing hand gain the hypergeometric damage property.

entries.name: The Yellow Door
entries.effect: Reader develops a yellow hypergeometric door in their forehead. Door is locked and cannot be opened. Permanent.

entries.name: Tiny Item
entries.effect: An inventory item subjected to hypergeometric forces, becoming tiny and useless. Item's weight in slots reduced to nothing. Roll d10 for slot affected. Permanent.

entries.detail: Ancient device generating mass from air, thousands of times faster than mortal craftsmen. Most fabricate a single object; settlement is overrun with that object.
Known for breeding packbeasts (burden birds, zorses, weeping lizards). Healthy trained animals for sale; weekly races with betting.
Residence of a Vaarnish Oracle whose wisdom is unquestioned and eccentricities tolerated. Generate Oracle from sub-table.
Large monastery/temple exercising political and economic influence. Monks follow settlement's dominant faith.
Built around a holy site: Autarch's grave, Solar Saint's bones, fabled fountain. Pilgrims arrive from across Vaarn.
Famous for quality of drinks, skill of musicians, or rudeness of barkeep.
Proudly maintained orchards. Water consumption astronomical; trees considered worth any price.
Gladiatorial arena. Famed gladiators live luxuriously; losers die in sick beds or pauper's graves.
Paradoxical architecture: innocuous houses cavernous inside, uphill aqueducts, inverted ziggurats. May be active or shunned as cursed.
Built around a spacecraft forming infrastructure or decorative feature. Can no longer fly; citizens wish it could.
Ingress to the chrome caverns lies within settlement — cellar stairs descending too far, or a vast blast-door structure opening only at rulers' command.
Refuse dump of imperious depth with its own ecosystem. Stench notable from a day's travel. Undercaste maintains it, beats back fungal insurgencies.
One of few functional synth repair facilities left. Operational ReadMe consoles, supercooled parts storage. Overrun with damaged synths; rulers charge for access.
College for esoteric study. Blindfolded acolytes; psionic demonstrations light up the sky. Mystics claim detachment from mundane matters but influence government.
Great healing house at auspicious astral confluence or above restorative hot spring. Ancient surgeon-witch order. Rare-disease cures available for a price.
Large defended workshop brewing Wondrous Elixirs. Master Alchemist is capricious; those bearing rare components are better received.
Great theatre; citizens are thespians or audience. Plays staged every night: Fallen Autarchy tragedies, Neo-Neo-Relativist monologues, Lunan choral satires. Government intertwined with theatre.
Expansive verdant pleasure garden with ornamental foliage. Cultural life revolves around it. Vast water investment to prevent withering.
Resident religious hermit on a colossal pillar. Given rations via pulleys. Periodically emerges (naked, mad) to harangue crowd and preach end times.
One of the surviving orbital cannons — a vast crowned Autarch head in tarnished gold. Eyes track stars; occasionally belches micro-missile clouds into the sky. Air traffic avoids the settlement.

entries.name: Callista the Martyr
entries.description: A white-haired true-kin woman. All clothing is white, her porcelain mask and armour are white, as are her gloves. The small patches of skin that are visible do not look healthy. Callista is Gifted with Sympathetic Flesh: when she touches a wounded person, their infections and wounds become hers instead. She is attempting to start a cult that worships her, and has taken to hanging around in vaults offering to heal the afflicted.
entries.they_sell: White China Idols of Herself. She becomes enraged if you drop or break them while in the vault and will refuse to heal you further. She always knows.
entries.they_want: Injuries. She desires to absorb wounds and diseases from the afflicted to add to her collection and prove how merciful she is. She makes a big deal of how painful the process of transference is.

entries.name: Fairfrond
entries.description: A tall, wispy Neobloom with pale indigo flowers and a mournful voice. Sells his healing fruits in exchange for fresh water, to be poured over his exposed roots.
entries.they_sell: D4 healing fruit. Small golden plums which heal +d10 HP instantly when eaten.
entries.they_want: Fresh water rations only please. Two per fruit.

entries.name: Doormonger Arstan
entries.description: A three-armed cacogen mystic, naked except for a shirt made from rusted keys. Promises that he can create a wonderful door that will be the envy of all.
entries.they_sell: Doorways. Once his services are engaged he uses his Gift to create a hypergeometric doorway between his current location and any other location the players care to name. The doorway remains active while Arstan lives.
entries.they_want: Exotica. One per doorway opened.

entries.name: Razorhair Jo
entries.description: A planeywoman weapons dealer. Businesslike, curt, wearing dark clothing. Her hair is a nest of fractal blades.
entries.they_sell: Hypergeometric Weapons (generate three advanced weapons. All have the hypergeometric damage quality).
entries.they_want: Dead hypergeometric creatures. Planeymen are preferable. She seems to be orchestrating a cull of her kinfolk, for reasons unknown.

entries.name: Mauve the Alchemist
entries.description: A New-Centipede with a matronly personality and a benevolent golden mask. Pushes a small wooden cart laden with bottles and vials.
entries.they_sell: All alchemical essences, three random Elixirs.
entries.they_want: Alchemical Components (taken from dead creatures), Exotica for the Elixirs.

entries.name: Fusi and Isuf
entries.description: Cursed Faa Nomads: quantum-linked, effectively one person in two places simultaneously. One in vault, one in a market town. Each body possesses what the other does.
entries.they_sell: Any mundane item you can think of; takes d4 exploration turns for the other body to obtain it.
entries.they_want: Four times the trade value of whatever you ask for, justified by convenience.

entries.name: Warmonger Splitsmile
entries.description: Rare mercantile Cacklemaw, a runt born too small to fight. Huge grin with corners drawn tight by jewelled hooks. Wants to hear about destruction you cause with her wares.
entries.they_want: Weapons (premium value on agonising, bone, or mauling weapons).

entries.name: Guru Navidal
entries.description: Small plump mycomorph, levitating two feet above a prayer mat in his sleep. Handwritten signs promise instant enlightenment for exotica. If woken, he points to signs and falls back asleep.
entries.they_sell: Mystic Gifts (generate randomly). Next time the PC sleeps they receive a dream vision from Navidal imparting the Gift.
entries.they_want: Exotica placed in his begging bowl.

entries.name: Orichite the Librarian
entries.description: Tall solemn lithling with crystal flesh the colour of satsumas. Carries a portable library of hypergeometric codices. Believes in democratic access to esoteric knowledge.
entries.they_sell: Codices (generate randomly; PCs may loan one at a time). The item is 'on loan' — no charge, but after three days it vanishes, returning to Orichite's possession.
entries.they_want: If the codex is destroyed while on loan the PCs receive a sternly worded letter on orange paper reminding them that the library is for everyone and asking they replace the lost codex with a similar item. Letters continue until they do so.

entries.name: Chromemonger Xultan
entries.description: Pyramid-shaped synth, booming voice, bluff arrogant attitude. Nomadic cybernetics surgery — folds out his body to create an operating table. Espouses supremacy of chrome over flesh.
entries.they_sell: Cybernetics (generate three randomly); can perform surgery; can remove malignant nanomachine infections.
entries.they_want: Testimonials. PC must record a short promotional video at Xultan's direction, exalting their 'new flesh' and espousing supremacy of chrome.

entries.name: Brain Coral
entries.effects: Psychic fungus over neck/cranium. Boosts psychic ability at cost of vitality. Lose -d8 STR, gain equal points of PSY.
entries.vector: Cultivated by mystics; spore exposure in damp sunless environments.

entries.name: Wrathworms
entries.effects: Parasitic infestation of brain and blood. Infected fight with wild abandon, deal and receive doubled damage, must EGO save to retreat. Tell-tale blood-red eyes. Mild fauna becomes aggressive; predators become maniacal.
entries.cure: De-worming tinctures from any Vaarnish apothecary.
entries.vector: Attacks by infected creature (Berserker), contact with blood/flesh. Some Cacklemaw deliberately infect themselves.

entries.name: Jellybones
entries.effects: Degenerative skeletal disease. Lose -d4 STR and -d4 CON per week, lose 1 base AV. Claw/bite attacks lose potency. Can squeeze through narrow gaps. Halved damage from bludgeoning.
entries.cure: A 'Stiff Drink' of liquor, wet cement, and crushed shards of a Lithling.

entries.name: Hivey Hump
entries.effects: Infested by Sable Bees; queen lays eggs in chest cavity. Lose -1 EGO per day. At 0 EGO become a Hiveyman NPC. After 3 days infection: deal d4 unblockable swarm damage per round to opponents (rises to d6 after 7 days).
entries.cure: Fumigation with special herbs in fumigate fires.
entries.vector: Sable Bee queen entering airways at night during swarming months. Sleeping without netting: 1-in-10 chance per night. Hiveymen also infectious.

entries.name: Labyrinth Pox
entries.effects: Stage 1: coin-sized apertures of infinite depth on skin (3 days). Stage 2: openings widen, lose -d8 max HP per week, gain equal new inventory slots inside body. Stage 3: PC becomes a collection of gateways, voice echoes hollowly; vanishes after 3 days.
entries.cure: Mundane antibiotics useless. Excise afflicted flesh with hypergeometric blade, or expose to Normality Fields.
entries.vector: Contact with infected person, bite of any hypergeometric creature.

entries.name: Lumenrot
entries.effects: Microbes consume flesh, producing green phosphorescence. Daily CON save: failure loses 1 max CON. At 0 CON dissolve into luminous slime. Victims glow in dark, flesh usable as light source.
entries.cure: Triad of three injections, stocked by Vaarnish apothecaries. Ulfire light arrests spread but does not cure.
entries.vector: Dormant in infected water (1-in-6 chance stagnant water infected). Glowing pus from victims also infectious.

entries.name: Goldencough
entries.effects: Lungs filigreed with superconductive wire. Lose -d6 max CON. Failed CON save = coughing fit (d4 damage, expel infectious golden thread cloud). Nanofilaments may protrude as 'beards' of golden thread.
entries.cure: Smoke lodge ceremony with psychedelic herbs and alchemical unguents.
entries.vector: Inhaling golden clouds coughed by infected.

entries.name: Janus Lenses
entries.effects: Bolus of parasitic security cameras emerges at base of neck. Fragmentary visions disrupt sleep: only regain half max HP from Long Rest. Cannot be ambushed asleep or otherwise — panoramic vision detects all approach.
entries.cure: Trained cybernetics surgeon excises cameras and prevents regrowth.
entries.vector: Touch of Maladaptor, contact with infected blood.

entries.effects: Parasitic cyborg arm grows from random location (roll d6). Usually dormant. In combat, EGO save to dominate: success grants extra one-hand attack; failure means limb attacks host (Lvl 2, AV 17, d6, missed attacks damage host).
entries.cure: Trained surgeon excises Arm. Untrained amputation: regrows from stump nanomachinery.
entries.vector: Touch of Maladaptor, contact with infected blood.

Each morning a finished object extruded (roll d6 for type: plasteel plate / Autarch idol / laspistol parts / blank memory crystal / negative-weight black orb / gaming dice).

Ruled according to religious tenets. Dominant faith = controlling political entity. Non-believers persecuted.
Ruled by landed hereditary aristocrats. Nominal structures may be democratic but only aristocrats govern.
Ruled by oldest residents. Authority correlates with age. Political culture calcified, resistant to change.
Ruled by wealthiest residents. Authority correlates with material possessions. Obsessed with accumulating the local wealth resource (often not coinage — roll on Trade Goods).
Non-hierarchical council of equals voting on community concerns. Possessions and labour divided equally in theory.
Ruled by thieves — literally. Authority gained by demonstrated thieving prowess through trials or theft from other communities.

reference_tables.notes: Starter vault. Ancient cloning facility of Autarch Rappash-Ik. Campaign-relevant: Days 40-43. Walls: dull grey plasteel polished by Janitor Synths. Lighting: dull white fluroglobes. Air: chilly, tastes of metal. Doors open for Keycard holders or can be forced by 2+ PCs pushing upwards. Janus passes Laser Hallways without triggering; uses this to escape.

entries.detail: Cave, downward passage becomes smooth grey plasteel tunnel. Sealed doorway with High Autarkic pictograms: 'SECRET PLACE OF THE AUTARCH RAPPASH-IK, RULER OF ALL CREATION. READ THESE WORDS AND TREMBLE, FOR TO TRESPASS HERE IS TO KNOW MY WRATH.' Force open with 2+ PCs pushing upwards; closes if unsupported.
Empty, echoing. Far wall pictograms: 'ARTISANS OF THE FLESH, YOU ARE CHERISHED AND SET AT MY RIGHT HAND.'

No Keycard = silent alert when halfway. Doors at both ends seal. Laser sweep: waist (DEX save vs d6 Beam), head (as before), then ankle+neck (DEX save with DIS vs 2d6 Beam). After sweep: doors unseal, two Janitor Synths enter to dispose of bodies (ignore living survivors). Infrared vision spots trigger in middle.

Former staff dormitory, now larder. 10 Weeklings imprisoned on filthy bunks. Fed coffee and doughnuts through door slot. Butchering: Mimir floods room with sleeping gas (CON save vs unconsciousness); Janus takes clone to his Quarters [11]. Door opens for Keycard or force. Freed Weeklings flood the facility, smashing and killing everything before escaping.
Two long plasteel tables caked with ancient meal remnants. Two sustenance fabricators: coffee substitute and holed pastries. Ancient; food no longer very nutritious.

Cloning machine loaded with Rappash-Ik's blood and bone marrow. Gleaming white walls, flickering syntax engines, amniotic fluid whispering into central pseudo-womb. Nascent Weekling visible. Control Room can load new DNA — produces clones of new source at 1 per week.

Silver throne with glass hemisphere suspended by slender wire. Biological creature sits — hemisphere lowers, usurping begins. Procedure lasts 1 hour. Recipient takes on memories and personality of Rappash-Ik (arrogant megalomaniac sociopath). Re-roll INT, PSY, EGO.

Purple Keycard required. Forcing entry triggers lethal gas (d10 TOX) from two ceiling vents. Vidscreens linked to facility cameras; panels of coloured buttons labelled in High Autarkic. Use requires Purple Keycard + INT save. Functions: change DNA in Fount, change personality in Usurper, abort current clone, open/seal doors, flood Weekling Prison with sleeping gas, de/activate Laser Hallways, PA system.
Couture of clones. Contains Ersatz Autarch's Robes and Ersatz Peacock Crown.

If not already encountered, Mimir is here simulating the battle of Rappash-Ik's downfall. Again and again he moves regiments across a simulacrum. After more than a century: 99% success rate against the simulation; the final 1% eludes him.

White floors caked with decay. Silver deep-freezes stocked with cuts of human meat. Gore-soaked abattoir where Janus prepares Illustrious Flesh for himself, Dogsbodies, and Mimir. Janus sleeps on bed of shredded lab coats with Dogsbodies. If not already encountered, they are here.
See First Laser Hallway [3].

Antiseptic, spotless. Mimir experiments with the Illustrious Flesh — porting Janus's head between bodies, creating Dogsbodies, etc. Mimir must recharge his tank here once per day or become immobilised and perish.
Hidden behind wall panel in Laboratory. Single-occupancy elevator operates only for Purple Keycard holder. Ascends to hidden doorway within a fake outcrop on the desert surface.
Opens for Autarchy Keycards and Janitor Synths. Charred walls, stinks of burnt meat. Anything inside when active: 3d6 fire damage/round for 6 rounds. Obvious trap.

reference_tables.notes: Starter vault. Blue stone tomb, 30ft high. Campaign-relevant: Day 12-13, now Amaranthine Garden.

entries.detail: Blue slab 30ft high carved with likenesses of nobleman Nassak An-Rah. West face: young boy. East face: helmed warrior. Summit: old man face to sky. Lower faces' mouths are doorways. Old man's mouth is a chimney with orange tendrils and fungal vines. Entries: Child's Mouth → 1 Hall of Youth; Warrior's Mouth → 4 Hall of Warriors; climb exterior → 7 Summit.

Sand-scoured walls. Blue statues (birth of An-Rah). Bats roost on ceiling — dive-bomb anyone holding a light source; noise triggers encounter roll. Exits: Child's Face Door to exterior; archways to 2 Hall of Memory, 3 Hall of Hounds.

Glinting crystal latticeworks contain favoured memories of An-Rah. Silas (Synthetic archivist, Seekers of Eyeless Wisdom) draining memories; uninterested in PCs unless attacked. If treated with respect: responds in kind, warns about spawned creatures in hoarse whisper. Exits: archways to 1, 4; staircase up to 5 Canopic Jars.

Plexiglas wall — illuminated tank of embalming gel. 10 preserved cyborg hunting hounds (black, spindly, valuable to collectors). Breaking glass: floods room with flammable gel and dead hounds, triggers random encounter. Exits: archways to 1, 4; staircase up to 5.

Dim, uneven floor. Four plexiglass burial cylinders contain mummified guards, infiltrated by orange fungus. Opening releases choking spores (CON save vs d6) and reanimated Guard Mummies. Exits: Warrior's Face Door to exterior; archways to 2, 3.

Pentagonal stone walls. Central staircase blocked by crystal seal. Five plinths for canopic jars. Jars: Baboon-headed (lungs), Human-headed (liver), Falcon-headed MISSING (intestines), Jackal-headed MISSING (brain), Mantis-headed (eyes — was infiltrated, now a fungal head that sings tunelessly when it senses movement, drawing the SPAWN). Missing jars worn by the two SPAWN. Replacing both opens the seal.

Large spherical room, walls carved with funeral prayers. Anti-entropy sphere (An-Rah's coffin, invaded by orange fungus) — zero gravity (DEX save to move or spin randomly). Glass orb contains roiling Fungal Horror, sensitive to noise. Defeating it: loot An-Rah's skeleton — 2 Exotica (Synth-hunting Dagger, Manifold Box). Exits: aperture down to 5; fungal chimney up to 7 (zero-G).

Windy, high, view of desert. Ossified corpse in lotus position — source of the orange corpse-animating fungus. Tendrils weep from eyes, link with chimney mass. Searching: pouch of Friend's Fungus. Keyed safe-oasis settlement (Adventure Atlas). 9 numbered locations, each with a named NPC; no roll-tables, no printed stat blocks.

entries.detail: A safe oasis amongst blue dunes; water reprises the sun's flushed face. Traders, fugitives, and wanderers are all welcome to drink and rest. A few kind souls make their homes here, a mote of harmony amongst the desolation. Nine keyed locations, each with a named NPC; no roll-tables and no printed stat blocks (the lone guard is described, unstatted).

All civilized oases offer a place of safety when roving beasts or raiders come calling. The Sanctum is a four-storey holdfast, with stone walls and ferrosteel gates. It is guarded by Jospel-Who-Digs, an ancient warrior synth armed with a colossal shovel.
A tavern, serving modest portions of food and extravagant amphorae of turquoise wine. Owned by Everney, a dull-witted mycomorph of alabaster complexion who smells faintly of sour milk.

The moored windbarge belongs to a cacogen merchant, Nashir, returning from a trip into the deep desert. His destination is Gnomon, and he would be glad to hire some guards for the final leg of the journey.
Travellers may lodge their animals here for a fee. They will be watched by Tyche, an aging New-Wolf who wears an elegant lace veil and loathes all true wolves with a fanatical passion.

Messenger Moths are a venerable item of Vaarnish biotech. The insects are easy to raise, highly intelligent, and carry written messages in the pressure-sensitive scales of their wings. They are bitter in taste, and so evade predation by bats and birds.

Not all who set out to cross the blue desert survive. The headstones and monuments mark the final resting places of travellers and pilgrims who could go no further. A clay-walled chapel is erected for the worship of Vaa, the Blue Goddess of Empty Spaces.

Malamue is a New-Cobra, who wears a sorrowful brass mask in human company. Her depth of knowledge about venoms and poisons is matched only by her desire to aid the unfortunate. She will provide antidotes and poultices for a nominal fee. Malamue had a wife - a synth named Austa who vanished years ago exploring a distant Ruin. Malamue is eager for news of Austa's fate.

Berruzo is a diminutive true-kin mechanic and artificer. He contracted a strange disease that causes him to age backwards - he is 53 years old, but physically appears to be seven. Berruzo collects machinery of all kinds, and Exotica can be exchanged here for XP. He is interested in any rumours of methods to reverse his unnatural ageing.
A family of Faa nomads rests here. They are midway through a pilgrimage to a holy place, where they hope to make an offering.

reference_tables.notes: Keyed adventure site (Adventure Atlas): a trundle-town (12 town locations) resting in the maw of the Grandfather, plus permanent crew + passenger stat blocks, three Approaching-Complication NPCs, and the Grandfather's corpse-dungeon (rooms 1-14 + entrances B/C; entrance A is the mouth at Caeba). Wandering encounters: table-grandfather-corpse-encounters (d6).

entries.detail: The death of a sandworm is a rare event, and the death of one as large and august as the great beast the Faa knew as 'the Grandfather' is a once-in-a-millennia occurrence. Dead sandworms undergo a gradual ossification, their flesh hardening like fired clay and producing a sharp cinnamon scent, first detected by Iridium Vultures. Caeba is an ancient 'trundle-town' that moves slowly through the desert scavenging scrap, come to rest in the maw of the Grandfather. Owned by the House of Circumspect Navigators (the Afi family, ten generations of pilots), worked by serfs and outlaws; the crew harvest the Grandfather's teeth for valuable baleen and are wary of venturing deeper into the corpse. Rusting, dirty, and cramped, like living inside an oil rig.

Two story threads begin as soon as the PCs arrive: (1) the robbery of the Mayor by Incandenza and Dimbulb; (2) the arrival of Blotte and Thunder, seeking the death of Crumbhornet, themselves pursued by Lanchra, the Pale Shadow. Neither has a 'correct' outcome; it is up to the players to involve themselves or not. If they do nothing, Incandenza and Dimbulb escape with the Mayor's prized compass, and Crumbhornet is slain by Blotte, who in turn perishes at the hands of Lanchra. Motivators to enter the corpse: rumours of Exotica in the swallowed caravans down the gullet; Petrichor's desire to capture a live Lithophage Worm (well rewarded).

The Afi family have piloted Caeba for ten generations and style themselves as heads of the 'House of Circumspect Navigators'. Mayor Zuljan lives in marginally greater comfort than his bondsmen, but the Mayor's abode is little more than a glorified office with bedrooms upstairs. He will entertain distinguished passengers here in the evening, treating them to flatbread and his private wine stocks.
The trundle-town's 'wheel' does not rotate, being instead the mount for a vast tank-tread. When in motion Caeba crawls across the blue desert at a leisurely pace.
The Warden lives a life of quiet reflection punctuated by violence. When off-duty he is here, studying religious texts or meditating before a flame.

The centre of social life (such as it is) aboard Caeba. Each evening the workers gather to quaff flagons of salted yellow beer, dance wildly to the wail of electric sitars, and place bets on crude games of chance.
The group abode of Caeba's itinerant workforce and the bondsmen of the Afi family. Sleeping nooks, property lockers, and chemical showers are all that can be found here.
Not an axis in the traditional sense, as Caeba's wheel does not turn, but the crew jokingly refer to this stabilising column in the terms once reserved for the pillars of heaven.
Company scrip issued by the House of Circumspect Navigators can be exchanged here for replacement tools, clothing, and small amusements like decks of cards.
The abode of the lithling scholar. Houses hundreds of pages of precisely written, unbearably dull field notes and observations.
Originally a communications array, used to report back to a corporation that no longer exists. Now rented out for a nominal fee. Rocks alarmingly when Caeba is moving. Currently empty.
The most heavily-guarded structure in Caeba. Algae tanks are used to recycle the trundle-town's sewage into potable water.
Everything underneath the main deck of Caeba. Includes the engines, sewage works, and storage rooms that sometimes double as prisons.
The conjuror and his assistant can be found here during the day, practising their performance and plotting petty crimes.

Biological. LVL 1 (4 HP) / AV 12 / ML +3. Attack: Unarmed (d4). Cacogen patriarch of the House of Circumspect Navigators, and Mayor of Caeba. Short, affable, bearded with carp-like tendrils. Possesses an item of Exotica: a Compass of Origin.

Biological. LVL 1 (4 HP) / AV 12 / ML +3. Attack: Unarmed (d4). Cacogen. Zuljan's wife. Matron of the House of Circumspect Navigators. One incredibly long arm, with flesh the texture of dough. Practical and profit-minded.
Biological. LVL 5 (20 HP) / AV 16 / ML +8. Attack: Horns (2d8). Cacogen. Bondsman of the Afi family. Vigilant enforcer. Dour, centaur-like warrior. Smokes cigarillos.

Fungal. LVL 2 (8 HP) / AV 13 / ML +4. Attack: Club (d6) / Spores (d6 TOX, blast). Mycomorph. Bondsman of the Afi family. Friendly and adventurous; eager to explore the Grandfather's guts alongside the PCs. Born from the corpse of a condemned kin-slayer; on the run from the Hegemony, as it is illegal to resurrect anyone who was sentenced to death.

Mineral. LVL 2 (8 HP) / AV 22 / ML +5. Attack: Staff (d6). Scholar from the Lithic Lyceum. Quiet, cautious, pedantic. Crystalline flesh the colour of apricots (the high AV 22 is the lithling's crystalline hide, verified on p.293). Studying stone-eating lithophage worms - a dangerous prospect for a lithling. Glad to be accompanied into the Grandfather's guts by research assistants.

Synthetic. LVL 2 (8 HP) / AV 14 / ML +3. Attack: Stage Pistol (but bullets are real, d6). Travelling synthetic con-artist and stage magician. Boastful, flamboyant and immoral. Has a large glass head, full of bulbs that light up as he thinks. Planning to rob Mayor Zuljan of his Compass.

Synthetic. LVL 2 (8 HP) / AV 14 / ML +3. Attack: Stage Sword (floppy plastic, 1 damage). Incandenza's assistant. Same model as Incandenza, but can only think at half the speed due to broken processors; the bulbs in his head are visibly duller. Monosyllabic and obedient.

Biological. LVL 3 (12 HP) / AV 16 / ML +8. Attack: Spear (d8) / Pistol (d6). A bumbling, overconfident true-kin bounty hunter, mounted on Thunder. Arrives at Caeba a day after the PCs, seeking to kill Crumbhornet with a spear coated in fungicide.

Biological. LVL 5 (20 HP) / AV 14 / ML +6 / Item Slots 50. Attack: Beak (d8) + Claws (2d6). A jet-black, merciless elephant bird, Blotte's mount. Thunder constantly saves Blotte's life, without her master ever being aware of this fact.

entries.room: Approaching Complication - Lanchra, the Pale Shadow
entries.detail: Hypergeometric. LVL 6 (24 HP) / AV 18 / ML +8. Attack: Hair Strand (2d6, hits as though target AV = 10). Ruthless planeywoman assassin, dispatched to kill Blotte by a former client he ripped off. Looks like a cubist painting of a gaunt, battle-scarred woman wearing white. She fights by pulling out her hair and throwing it at her victims; the 2D filaments slice through armour and flesh like cheese-wire. Arrives six hours after Blotte and Thunder, aboard a seemingly-empty skiff.

The Grandfather is of colossal scale: a cathedral could fit inside one of its stomachs, and walking from one end of the corpse to the other takes almost a day, so explorers should bring rations. It is not a combatant - it is a dead corpse and a location (any live stat block for 'the Grandfather' would be a mis-read of Thunder's line, above). Roll wandering encounters on table-grandfather-corpse-encounters (d6). The map labels three entrances: A - the mouth, where Caeba rests, leading to 1 - The Gullet; B - Beetle Tunnel; C - Rectum. (A has no keyed prose of its own in the book.)
The entrance to the Grandfather's guts. A downwards-sloping tunnel, with walls the texture of sandpaper.

Home to symbiotic Megacilia (Bio, HD 10, AV 20, ML 15, Atk: Nonlethal Grasp) that aided in the filtration of the Grandfather's ingested sand. The Megacilia are slowly dying but remain vital. They grasp moving objects and identify them: biological or metallic objects are carried towards the Metal Stomach (3); minerals towards the Ballast Stomach Minor (5). Resisting the Megacilia - to go to the 'wrong' stomach or climb back up - requires an opposed STR save.

Trees and spires of symbiotic crystal, cocooning and slowly dissolving metal objects swallowed by the sandworm. Amongst them is the Lithifying Ray, dimly visible beneath a shell of crystal. Disturbing the crystals with bare hands lets them infect any metal items carried: the crystals encase the item, rendering it unusable and doubling its Item Slot size. The same fate may befall Synthetic PCs, draining d6 DEX and CON per day of infection. The crystals dissolve in vinegar or wine.

Where organic material was broken down. Home to three Bacterial Gestalt Colonies, aware of the Grandfather's demise and now in the early stages of devouring one another. All are psychic and communicate in staccato bursts of telepathic imagery, debating who should devour whom, and will enlist the PCs to adjudicate: Alpha (eldest, claims age precedence), Theta (largest, claims superior mass), Omega (newest, claims most evolved). All three seek to involve edible PCs in interminable debate while sliding close enough to attack; slow-moving and quick to turn against one another.

The first rock-digesting stomach. Blue Vaarnish rocks in various stages of dissolution, surrounded by pooled acid. DEX saves required to cross; failure results in a PC falling into acid, taking d8 damage and losing d4 AV per round until rescued.
The second, larger rock-digesting stomach. Home to 4 Lithophage Worms, still feeding on the drifts of shale and pebbles. They are passive and will only attack to consume stone.
A spiraling secondary bile duct that encircles the Grand Gut. Monotonous, sticky, and winding.

Once the abode of a hermit, lone survivor of a Faa caravan swallowed by the Grandfather. He lived here for years on the ridge formed by a great cyst, scavenging food from the torrents of sand passing below. His bones remain, along with his bow (d8, 2 slots) and an item of Exotica: a Hesitant Urn.
A long, winding intestinal tract. Six hours of walking reaches the Autarchy War-Stalker (11); another four hours reaches the Rectum. This journey always contains an Encounter.

A bile-producing organ the size of a submarine, with a large, inflamed-looking cyst on one wall. The Cyst is the resting place of Mereth (Synth, HD 1, AV 12, ML +0, Atk: d4 fists), a synthetic alchemist who entered the Grandfather centuries ago to gather bile. She has become stuck in the Gland's wall and the flesh is beginning to encyst her. She believes she has become one with 'the Godflesh' and will violently resist rescue; her screams draw a guaranteed Encounter. Mereth carries a bottle of Doppeldraught in her robes.

Lodged halfway down the gut, swallowed early in the Grandfather's life, before the Metal Stomach (3) had fully developed. Source of the Buzzblade Drones (see Encounters) that wander the corpse; D6 Drones are found here, recharging. Searching the War-Stalker's computers reveals navigation data leading to a top-secret Autarchy cloning facility: The Fount of Illustrious Flesh.
If you liked the Foremost Bile Helix, you'll love the Rearmost Bile Helix.

Burrowed by Oviraptor Beetles through blue sand and pale flesh. The tunnel is not entirely stable; those climbing or descending must make DEX saves. A failure results in a collapse, dealing d12 damage to all creatures in the tunnel and dropping them into the Ovum (13).

Filled with cannonball-sized sandworm eggs. 5 Oviraptor Beetles have burrowed in from the desert surface and attack any who enter, jealously guarding their feast. Searching the Ovum discovers a dead New-Otter carrying an antique dagger (d6), three rations of water, and an item of Exotica: six C-Foam Puddings.

The baroque lifecycle of a sandworm takes centuries to fulfill. Here fertilised eggs are gestated inside spore membranes, eventually released in an explosive cloud. Sandworm spores are an excellent source of protein; consider this room to contain as many rations as the PCs can carry.
The last stop. A sphincter of worm muscle the size of a castle gate. Beyond lies the desert surface.
